name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,422

entries.clue: Compartment at bow, sailor home? (5)

indicatorNotes.at bow: the bow is a ship's front, so the letter at the front of 'Compartment'

annotation.surface: Someone asks where a sailor lives aboard: in the room up at the front of the ship.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and a description of a sailor's cabin, which is why it ends with a question mark.
annotation.definitionFit: A cabin is a compartment on a ship where a sailor lives.

entries.clue: Man with leg over the Queen, European escort? (9)

blocks.note: in cricket the leg side is also called the on side

annotation.surface: A cheeky picture of a man getting his leg over the Queen, with a European acting as escort.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Leg over' is British slang for sex, which is the joke; the pieces simply join up in order. Leg = ON comes from cricket, where the leg side of the field is also the on side.
annotation.definitionFit: A chaperone is someone who escorts and supervises another person.

entries.clue: Head over for a riotously good time (5)

annotation.surface: Someone heads over to a place for a wild party.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Head over' reads as 'go there', but each word is a separate piece. A beano is British slang for a noisy party or celebration.
annotation.definitionFit: A beano is a lively, boisterous party.

entries.clue: Most geeky resident in need of a makeover (8)

indicatorNotes.in need of a makeover: a makeover remakes something, so the letters are to be rearranged

annotation.surface: The geekiest person in the building badly needs a new look.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a gentle insult about a neighbour's style, and the makeover is the rearranging of RESIDENT.
annotation.definitionFit: Nerdiest is the superlative of nerdy, meaning geekiest.

entries.clue: Top brass run wildly? Exercise restraint! (6,3)

indicatorNotes.wildly: the letters run wild, out of order

annotation.surface: Senior officers are running amok and someone tells them to show some self-control.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Exercise restraint' looks like advice to calm down; read as a noun phrase it is a restraint worn for exercise.
annotation.definitionFit: A sports bra is a supportive garment that restrains the bust during exercise.

entries.clue: Ooze sophistication at first, then continue going topless (4)

indicatorNotes.at first: what comes at first in a word is its opening letter, so only that is kept
indicatorNotes.topless: in a down answer the top is the first letter, so it comes off

blocks.note: KEEP (continue going) without its top letter K

annotation.surface: Advice to exude class at first, and then carry on without a top.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Keep going' means continue, so 'continue going' is KEEP, and losing its top leaves EEP.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: liquid that oozes trickles slowly through, exactly as it seeps.

entries.clue: Large señoritas excited old French right-wingers (10)

blocks.note: L = large, as on clothing labels

annotation.surface: A group of lively Spanish young women has somehow got a bunch of French royalists worked up.
annotation.walkthrough: The Orleanists backed the Orléans branch of the French royal family in the 19th century. Crosswords ignore accents, so the Ñ counts as N.
annotation.definitionFit: Orleanists were 19th-century French royalists, a right-wing faction.

entries.clue: Great shock to hear short old lady's stolen gold (6)

indicatorNotes.short: TRY is cut short by its last letter
indicatorNotes.'s stolen: the old lady has stolen the gold, so it is taken inside

blocks.note: to hear a case in court is to TRY it; short, it loses the Y
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

annotation.surface: Someone is shaken to learn that a little old woman has robbed some gold.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hear' is a judge's word here, not a listener's: a judge hears, or tries, a case. The old lady is Mum, and ''s' stands for 'has'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the psychological sense: an event so distressing it leaves lasting harm, which 'Great' signals.

entries.clue: Bishop in the can ... constipated? (7,2)

blocks.note: B = bishop, as in chess notation
'the can' is slang for prison, so in the can = locked up

annotation.surface: A bishop sits on the toilet, and the question is whether he is having trouble.
annotation.walkthrough: 'The can' means the toilet in the surface and prison in the wordplay. The bishop goes first, followed by being in prison.
annotation.definitionFit: An informal, bodily idiom: bowels that cannot move are described as stopped or jammed, like a drain.

entries.clue: Player about given up? Flipping nonsense! (5)

indicatorNotes.given up: in a down answer, sent up means turned to read bottom to top

annotation.surface: A performer who has quit is dismissed as a load of nonsense.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' reads as a mild British swear word, like 'blooming', but it is the second reversal instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: An older theatrical sense: Shakespeare's 'all the men and women merely players' means performers on a stage.

entries.clue: A moderate to deliver equitable treatment (1,4,4)

blocks.note: to deal is to deliver, as a blow or cards

annotation.surface: A political centrist is expected to hand out even-handed treatment.
annotation.walkthrough: 'A moderate' reads as a noun, a middle-of-the-road politician, but it splits into A plus FAIR used as an adjective.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: being given a just, even-handed arrangement is getting a square deal.

entries.clue: A duck-filled bath turned over roughly (5)

indicatorNotes.filled: the bath is filled with the duck, so O goes inside
indicatorNotes.turned over: turned upside down, so read backwards

blocks.note: a duck is a score of nought in cricket, O

annotation.surface: A bath with a duck in it has been knocked over carelessly.
annotation.walkthrough: The rubber duck in the bath is really a cricket duck, a score of zero, so O. BUT holds it after the B.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for an approximate figure: 'roughly ten' and 'around ten' say the same thing.

entries.clue: Sexy quote about men, all retired (6)

indicatorNotes.about: the quote goes around the men
indicatorNotes.all retired: everything withdraws, going back, so the whole is read backwards

annotation.surface: A saucy line about soldiers who have all left the service.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Retired' suggests pensioners; in wordplay it means going back, and 'all' makes the whole assembly turn round, not just the men.
annotation.definitionFit: Erotic means sexy, arousing desire.

entries.clue: A blow for one exploiting sunny weather? (8)

blocks.note: a wild, round-arm swinging punch, named for the scything motion of a farm worker
the proverb says make hay while the sun shines

annotation.surface: Bad luck for someone out enjoying the sunshine.
annotation.walkthrough: The second half plays on the proverb 'make hay while the sun shines': a haymaker literally makes hay, and is also one who seizes a chance.
annotation.definitionFit: A haymaker is a powerful swinging blow with the fist.

entries.clue: American's bright idea for British power shower? (10)

blocks.note: the American word for what the British call a brainwave, a sudden inspiration
brain power coming down like a storm; in British use, a sudden mental upheaval

annotation.surface: An American thinks a power shower is a clever British invention.
annotation.walkthrough: A power shower is a British name for a high-pressure electric shower. Read cryptically, it is a shower of brain power: a storm of the brain.
annotation.definitionFit: Americans call a sudden bright idea a brainstorm, where the British say brainwave.

entries.clue: Tax too much? Done with society? Then teach! (10)

annotation.surface: A string of questions from someone overtaxed and fed up with the world, deciding to take up teaching.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tax' here means to put a strain on, not to charge money. 'Done with society' reads as dropping out; it is OVER plus S.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the sense of burdening: to tax a muscle or a mind is to strain it, and too much is over.

entries.clue: Put out some Zinfandel, I'm in a temper! (9)

indicatorNotes.some: only some of the letters of the phrase are used, a run inside it

blocks.note: the run starts at the last two letters of Zinfandel and stops two letters into temper

annotation.surface: Someone angrily orders a bottle of red wine put out.
annotation.walkthrough: Zinfandel is a red wine grape. The answer runs across four words and ignores the apostrophe.
annotation.definitionFit: A sporting sense: a team knocked out of a cup has been put out of it.

entries.clue: Nice lady stripped the first guy to come along (4)

annotation.definition: the first guy to come along

indicatorNotes.stripped: stripped of its outer layer, so its first and last letters

blocks.note: MADAME, a lady in Nice, France, without its outer letters

annotation.surface: A woman on the Riviera undresses for the first man who happens by.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Nice' is the French city, so its lady is a MADAME. 'The first guy to come along' reads as any passer-by, but Adam was literally the first man.
annotation.definitionFit: In Genesis, Adam is the first man to exist.

entries.clue: Mass reunites awfully Christian-minded folk? (9)

indicatorNotes.awfully: the letters are put together badly

annotation.surface: A church Mass brings back together a flock of devout believers.
annotation.walkthrough: Christian here is Fletcher Christian, who led the mutiny on the Bounty; his followers were of his mind. Mass, reunites and Christian all point to church.
annotation.definitionFit: Fletcher Christian's followers on the Bounty were mutineers.

entries.clue: Fixed to keep punching one such as Corbyn (8)

indicatorNotes.punching: a punch goes into its target, so STORE goes inside

blocks.note: Jeremy Corbyn, a left-wing former Labour Party leader, is a red

annotation.surface: A plot is set to keep hitting a left-wing politician.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fixed' suggests rigged, but here it means repaired. 'One such as Corbyn' asks for a type he belongs to: a red, a left-winger.
annotation.definitionFit: Something fixed has been restored to working order.

entries.clue: Go off sex - it's not all that! (4)

indicatorNotes.not all that: not all of the words are used, only letters inside them

blocks.note: drop the outer S at each end and the letters between are the answer

annotation.surface: Someone is losing interest in sex, which isn't all it's cracked up to be.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Not all that' is slang for overrated, and it doubles as the instruction to take only part of 'sex - it's'.
annotation.definitionFit: To exit is to go off, as an actor leaves the stage.

entries.clue: To satisfy craving, southern dons smoke some weed (3,3,4)

indicatorNotes.dons: to don is to put on, so the phrase wraps round S like clothing

blocks.note: take a hit of the pot, cannabis

annotation.surface: Southern university lecturers light up a joint to deal with their cravings.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Dons' looks like university teachers but is the verb: to put on. HIT THE POT wears S between THE and POT.
annotation.definitionFit: Something that hits the spot satisfies exactly what you were craving.

entries.clue: Putting in stuffing, having removed pigeon's head (6)

indicatorNotes.having removed: the named letter is taken away

blocks.note: the first letter of pigeon, removed

annotation.surface: A cook stuffs a pigeon after cutting off its head.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a recipe, but the stuffing is PADDING, as in a cushion, and the pigeon only supplies its P.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: putting in an extra ingredient or a remark is adding it.

entries.clue: Briefly refrigerate babe? That's immature (8)

indicatorNotes.Briefly: cut short, so the last letter goes

blocks.note: a dish is an attractive person

annotation.surface: Someone scoffs at the idea of putting a baby in the fridge for a moment.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Babe' suggests a baby, which is why childish sits so snugly; in the wordplay it means an attractive person, a dish.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, used as a put-down: behaviour like a child's is immature.

entries.clue: Funny business with half-cut Hoskins in charge (5)

indicatorNotes.half-cut: half of the word is cut away

blocks.note: the setter Hoskins calls himself ME, and half of it is M

annotation.surface: The setter, a bit drunk, is running some comedy.
annotation.walkthrough: The setter's pseudonym stands for ME. 'Half-cut' is British slang for tipsy, and here it cuts ME in half.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym as an adjective: a comic turn or scene is one meant to be funny.

entries.clue: Old red mark, bit of lippy involved? (6)

indicatorNotes.involved: the L is caught up inside the mark

annotation.surface: A red smear on a collar, and a question whether lipstick is behind it.
annotation.walkthrough: The red mark looks like lipstick, but 'Old red' is the definition: a communist of the past. Lippy is British slang for lipstick.
annotation.definitionFit: Stalin was a Soviet communist leader, a red of old.

entries.clue: Fast, but not initially friendly, pork pie delivery? (5)

blocks.note: the first letter of friendly, removed

annotation.surface: A butcher's fast, friendly delivery of pork pies.
annotation.walkthrough: A pork pie is rhyming slang for a lie (a porky), so delivering pork pies is lying. FLYING is the wordplay's 'fast'.
annotation.definitionFit: Telling pork pies, or lies, is lying.

entries.clue: Just tops to see Hoskins in negligee, showing bit of leg (4)

indicatorNotes.Just tops: only the top letters, the first of each word in a down answer

blocks.note: the opening letter of each of the four words, read in order

annotation.surface: The setter pictures himself in a negligee, wearing only the top and flashing some leg.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Just tops' reads as a nightie with no bottoms, but it means only the first letters.
annotation.definitionFit: The shin is the front part of the lower leg.

entries.clue: City goal upset Messi, he's gutted! (5)

indicatorNotes.upset: in an across answer, overturned means read backwards
indicatorNotes.gutted: the insides are removed, so only the outer letters stay

annotation.surface: A football team concedes against Lionel Messi's side and he is devastated.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Gutted' is British for bitterly disappointed, and in wordplay it empties a word. Messi played for Inter Miami, which makes the scene apt.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the Florida city is one of many cities, and here the surface's football club is its clue.

entries.clue: Wet hero is to get changed or else! (9)

annotation.surface: A soaked hero is told to change clothes, or there will be trouble.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Or else' sounds like a threat tacked on, but it is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym as a conjunction: 'do it, otherwise you'll regret it' works with 'or else' swapped in.

entries.clue: Religious type my clanger annoyed (9)

annotation.surface: A vicar was irritated by my embarrassing blunder.
annotation.walkthrough: A clanger is British slang for a blunder, so the surface is a gaffe that upset a vicar.
annotation.definitionFit: A loose description: a priest or vicar ordained in a church is a religious type of person.

entries.clue: Painter editor repelled with flatulence (5)

annotation.surface: An artist drives away his editor by breaking wind.
annotation.walkthrough: Edgar Degas was the French painter of ballet dancers. The surface's joke is literal: the editor is repelled by the gas.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the French Impressionist famous for ballet dancers is one painter among many.
